$\int\left(\sec^{2}x + \sin x\right)dx$
$= \tan x + (-\cos x) + C$
$= \tan x - \cos x + C$

questions.question_text: A curve has gradient function $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sin x$ and passes through $(\pi,\, 4)$. Find the equation of the curve.

options.why: Evaluated $-\cos\pi$ as $-1$ rather than $+1$ when solving for $C$.
Used $\cos x$ as the primitive of $\sin x$, then solved $\cos\pi + C = 4$ to get $C = 5$.
Used $\cos x$ as the primitive of $\sin x$ but kept the constant found from the correct primitive.

questions.solution_text:
$y = \int\sin x\,dx$
$= -\cos x + C$
Substitute $x = \pi$ and $y = 4$.
$4 = -\cos\pi + C$
$4 = 1 + C$
$C = 3$
$y = -\cos x + 3$
